1. (Currently Amended) An optical physiological sensor integrated into a wearable device, the optical physiological sensor comprising:a substrate having an optical center;
a first emitter group of light emitting diodes (LEDs) positioned adjacent to the optical center of the substrate and spaced at an offset from the optical center;
a second emitter group of LEDs positioned adjacent to the optical center of the substrate at an offset to the optical center and spaced at an offset from the optical center opposite the first emitter group of LEDs relative to the optical center; and
a plurality of detectors arranged in a spatial configuration that surrounds the first and the second emitter group, wherein each of the plurality of detectors are positioned on the substrate a same distance away from the optical center of the substrate; and
a light barrier construct mounted on the substrate and defining a first emitter chamber that houses the first emitter group of LEDs, and a second emitter chamber that houses the second emitter group of LEDs, wherein the light barrier construct is configured to optically isolate the first emitter group of LEDs from the second emitter group of LEDs.
2. (Currently Amended) The sensor of Claim 1, wherein the spatial configuration is annular includes an annulus.
3. (Cancelled)
4. (Currently Amended) The sensor of Claim 1-3,wherein the light barrier construct includes a maximum height extending away from the substrate at the optical center of the substrate.
5. (Currently Amended) The sensor of Claim 1-3,wherein the light barrier construct comprises a light barrier configured to isolate the first emitter group from the second emitter group, wherein a width of the light barrier includes a width of isless than 1.40mm a distance from an emitter chamber defined by the light barrier construct and housing the first emitter group to a detector chamber defined by the light barrier construct and housing a detector bisected by a centerline of the sensor.
6. (Cancelled)
7. (Cancelled)
8. (Currently Amended) The sensor of Claim 1, wherein the first emitter group is configured to emit optical radiation having a same wavelength a same plurality of light wavelengths as optical radiation emitted from the second emitter group.
9. (Original) The sensor of Claim 1, wherein an arrangement of the LEDs of the first emitter group on the substrate mirrors an arrangement of the LEDs of the second emitter group on the substrate across a centerline of the sensor that bisects the sensor.
10. (Original) The sensor of Claim 9, wherein the centerline of the sensor bisects at least one of the plurality of detectors.
11. (Original) The sensor of Claim 10, wherein a distance from the first emitter group to the at least one of the plurality of detectors is substantially similar to a distance from the second emitter group to the at least one of the plurality of detectors.
12. (Original) The sensor of Claim 1, further comprising an ECG sensor, wherein the ECG sensor comprises a reference electrode, a negative electrode, and a positive electrode and wherein the reference and negative electrodes are located on the sensor and wherein the positive electrode is located on a housing of the wearable device.
13. (Original) The sensor of Claim 12, wherein the reference and negative electrodes are releasably coupled to the substrate of the sensor via one or more springs configured to bias the reference and negative electrodes away from the substrate.
14. (Original) The sensor of Claim 12, wherein the reference electrode is substantially semi-annular and wherein the negative electrode is substantially semi-annular.
15. (Original) The sensor of Claim 14, wherein the reference and negative electrodes surround the plurality of detectors.
16. (Original) The sensor of Claim 1, wherein the plurality of detectors includes a first detector group and a second detector group.
17. (Original) The sensor of Claim 16, wherein the first detector group includes at least two detectors housed in respective detector chambers, and wherein the second detector group includes at least two detectors housed in respective detector chambers.
18. (Original) The sensor of Claim 16, wherein a distance between the first emitter group and the first detector group is greater than a distance between the second emitter group and the first detector group.
Filing Date: July 12, 2022
19. (Original) The sensor of Claim 1, wherein the substrate comprises a printed circuit board (PCB).
20. (New) The sensor of Claim 2, wherein the annular spatial configuration has a radius of less than 6.75mm.
